handbookNote: New Mexico Commercial Driver License Manual (base AAMVA '2005 CDL Testing System' content, Version: July 2017), published by the New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division (MVD), a division of the New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department (confirmed as the current administering agency via mvd.newmexico.gov and tax.newmexico.gov/about-us/motor-vehicle-division/ on 2026-08-23 -- no agency transition has occurred here, unlike some other states in this project) -- fetched directly from https://realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/2005%20CDL%20Driver%20Manual%20-July%202017%20-%20FINAL%202.pdf on 2026-08-23 (5.5MB PDF, linked from the official 'Download Manuals' and 'MVD Driver's License Manuals' pages on mvd.newmexico.gov, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/nm_cdl_research/nm_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,132 lines), supplemented by the standalone New Mexico MVD-11196 'CDL Licensing Information' addendum, fetched from https://realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/MVD11196.pdf on 2026-08-23 (extracted to scratchpad/nm_cdl_research/nm_cdl_addendum_full.txt), and cross-referenced against the official 'Chapter 5: Commercial Driver License' page of the MVD Driver Procedures Manual at https://www.mvd.newmexico.gov/chapter-5-commercial-driver-license/ (checked 2026-08-23). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are PARTIALLY CONFIRMED: the passing score is directly and explicitly stated in New Mexico's own official manual text (MVD-11196 front matter, embedded in the fetched manual PDF, Rev 8/17) -- 'Each part of the Knowledge and Skills Test is graded independently. A passing score is 80% or higher.' -- this is NOT hedged; it is a direct quote from an official NM.gov-hosted document, consistent with the federal 80% minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a). However, the exact NUMBER OF ITEMS per knowledge test (General Knowledge or any endorsement) is never disclosed anywhere in the fetched official New Mexico sources -- confirmed by exhaustive keyword search of the full extracted manual text for 'questions', 'item count', and similar terms, which surfaced no per-test question count. Per this project's no-default-values discipline, the practice-exam session length in this platform's config (EXAM_CONFIGS, set separately from this content build) follows the same 50-question/80%-minimum convention already used across other hedged-item-count CDL states in this project (consistent with the shared AAMVA base manual and third-party CDL test-prep convergence), but this specific item count is NOT asserted as an officially confirmed New Mexico figure anywhere in this question bank's source citations. New Mexico's own front-matter addendum also reveals two genuinely NM-specific structural quirks, both preserved rather than smoothed over: (1) New Mexico uses a NON-STANDARD FOUR-CLASS system (A, B, C, D) rather than the base AAMVA manual's federal three-class (A, B, C) framework -- NM's addendum defines a distinct Class D covering vehicles placarded for hazardous materials with a GVWR under 26,000 lbs, or vehicles designed to carry 16+ passengers, that the base manual's own Section 1 Introduction folds directly into its federal 'Class C' definition; this question bank documents NM's own 4-class framework as authoritative for New Mexico-specific licensing questions while still drawing safety-technical content from the shared base manual sections. (2) The addendum's own 'ENDORSEMENT / DESCRIPTION / WRITTEN TEST / SKILLS TEST' table renders with the DESCRIPTION column shifted down one row relative to the ENDORSEMENT letter column, a PDF-table-extraction artifact (verified identically present in both the embedded Rev 8/17 version and the standalone Rev 12/13 MVD-11196 PDF) -- resolved for question-drafting purposes by using the base AAMVA Section 1 Introduction's own unambiguous prose description of each endorsement (H-Hazardous Materials, N-Tank Vehicle, P-Passenger, S-School Bus, T-Doubles/Triples, X-combined Tank+Hazmat) as the authoritative source, not the garbled table. Additionally, two DIFFERENT versions of the MVD-11196 addendum were found and reconciled: the CURRENT version (Rev 8/17), embedded as front matter directly inside the officially linked manual PDF, states CDL knowledge tests 'can be taken no more than two (2) times in a 7 day period'; a separate, OLDER standalone MVD-11196 PDF (Rev 12/13) still linked from the same MVD download page states a different, superseded rule ('three times within a one year period' for knowledge tests). This question bank treats the newer Rev 8/17 embedded text as authoritative for the knowledge-test retest rule (consistent with it being the version actually bound into the current manual), and flags the discrepancy explicitly rather than silently picking one; the skills-test retest rule (three attempts within one year, then a one-year wait) is identical and uncontested in both versions. Restriction codes: the base manual's federal set of ten (E, K, L, M, N, O, P, V, X, Z) is supplemented in New Mexico's own addendum with three additional state-added restriction codes -- B (corrective lenses), C (mechanical aids), D (prosthetic aids) -- for a New-Mexico-specific total of 13 restriction codes, all sourced from the MVD-11196 addendum text itself. Content-depth rationale: New Mexico uses the identical AAMVA-authored 'CDL Driver's Manual, 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017' base document already used by several other CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Louisiana's officially hosted manual carries the exact same base-document title and version string), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering subsections 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.8 the Hazardous Materials Glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one bucket -- plus New Mexico-specific administrative detail (4-class licensing system, endorsements, restrictions, prequalification documents, ELDT requirements effective February 7, 2022, medical certification, retest rules, ss/passing score) layered into the licensing bucket from the manual's New Mexico-specific front matter (MVD-11196). Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Air Brakes, Hazardous Materials, and School Bus supported deeper coverage than initially targeted and were sized up accordingly. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official New Mexico manual/addendum text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake pressure thresholds, tank vehicle capacity figures, weight/class thresholds, retest timeframes) were verified against the actual New Mexico text read during drafting.
